questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: What is a golden query set?
options: A maintained, judged sample of representative information needs
Every query ever issued in production
Only queries on which the current system succeeds
A list of documents sorted by length

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: Why are production query logs a useful sampling frame?
options: They contain perfect relevance labels
They reveal actual wording, mistakes, identifiers, and ambiguity
They remove all privacy obligations
They guarantee equal coverage of rare intents

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: What problem does stratified query sampling address?
options: It makes every query equally frequent in production
It eliminates the need for aggregation weights
It preserves coverage of important classes that a uniform sample may underrepresent
It converts graded labels into binary labels

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: Why maintain both a stable core and a rotating recent slice?
options: To prevent assessors from seeing any old query
To make the test set smaller every quarter
To ensure every query has a click
To preserve longitudinal comparison while adapting to drift

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: Why is selecting only queries with clicks a biased construction rule?
options: It excludes abandonment and zero-result failures while reflecting incumbent exposure
Clicks always indicate irrelevance
Clicked queries cannot contain spelling errors
It produces too many multilingual queries

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets: Sampling Real Queries
questions.question: A rare compliance class is 1 percent of traffic but has high failure cost. What is the best test-set treatment?
options: Exclude it because macro metrics would be easier
Oversample it as a named stratum and retain weights for overall estimates
Duplicate frequent navigational queries instead
Give every compliance result grade 3 without judging

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: How is a relevance pool normally constructed?
options: By judging every document in the collection
By taking random characters from each result
By deduplicating top results contributed by multiple retrieval systems
By labeling only the incumbent's first result

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: What is the main reason to use pooling?
options: To ensure no document remains unjudged
To avoid defining relevance
To make every system return identical results
To focus limited judging effort on plausible relevant candidates

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: What is the primary tradeoff when increasing pool depth?
options: Coverage tends to improve while judgment cost grows
Both coverage and cost always decrease
Labels become binary automatically
Contributor diversity stops mattering

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: Why should assessors be blinded to contributor and original rank?
options: To keep document text hidden
To reduce expectations that could bias relevance grades
To prevent duplicate removal
To make judgments system-specific

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: A semantic retriever is evaluated on a pool built only from lexical systems. What is the central risk?
options: Its result scores must be negative
It cannot retrieve any shared documents
Its novel relevant documents may be unjudged and treated as irrelevant
Its queries become longer

questions.topic: Pooling: Judging Relevance Feasibly at Scale
questions.question: Which evidence best supports stopping pool expansion?
options: The pool has a round number of documents
One contributor wins every query
No assessor requested a break
Metric stability and audits show diminishing relevant yield from added candidates

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: How should an LLM relevance judge be treated?
options: As a measurement instrument requiring calibration
As infallible ground truth
As a replacement for the relevance rubric
As a ranking system that needs no labels

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: What should a judge prompt define explicitly?
options: Only the candidate's byte length
The relevance grades and criteria separating them
The final system leaderboard
A secret grade for each contributor

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: What does requiring passage evidence from an LLM judge help detect?
options: Index compression ratio
Query sampling weights
Rationales claiming support absent from the candidate
The number of benchmark datasets

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: Why should model identifier, prompt, and truncation settings be versioned?
options: They guarantee agreement with every human
They remove the need to cache inputs
They make all grades binary
Changes can shift labels and undermine reproducibility

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: A judge often upgrades human grade 2 to grade 3. Which metric setup can amplify the error most?
options: nDCG using exponential relevance gain
Binary result count with no relevance labels
Median query character length
Index size in bytes

questions.topic: LLM-as-Relevance-Judge: Uses and Failure Modes
questions.question: What is the strongest use of judge confidence in a production labeling workflow?
options: Accept every confident answer without testing
Route uncertain or high-impact cases to humans after validating calibration
Discard all low-confidence queries from evaluation
Use confidence as the relevance grade

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: What do public retrieval benchmarks primarily provide?
options: Proof of production suitability
Private user behavior for every product
Shared datasets, metrics, and comparison baselines
A guarantee against training-data contamination

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: What is a defining value of BEIR?
options: It contains only one homogeneous web corpus
It measures application latency directly
It supplies production labels for private data
It tests retrieval across heterogeneous datasets and domains

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: Why should BEIR results be reported per dataset as well as averaged?
options: An average can hide concentrated gains and domain-specific failures
Every dataset uses the same documents
Per-dataset scores eliminate all contamination
The average is never mathematically defined

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: What happens when a public test split is repeatedly used to select prompts and checkpoints?
options: It becomes more representative of production automatically
It effectively becomes development data and performance can be overfit
Its judgments become exhaustive
Its resource cost becomes irrelevant

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: A model improves benchmark nDCG but makes retrieval one hundred times slower. What is the correct conclusion?
options: It must replace the production system
Latency never matters in retrieval
The relevance gain must be evaluated against the product's resource and latency constraints
The benchmark score should be multiplied by one hundred

questions.topic: Public Benchmarks in Context: MS MARCO and BEIR
questions.question: Which evaluation sequence provides the strongest evidence?
options: Tune only on the public test set
Use only a private set with no baseline checks
Report one benchmark average without configuration
Reproduce baselines, test heterogeneous benchmarks, then validate on a product-specific golden set
